findings.title: migrations-log entry 122 still closes its mandatory-preflight paragraph with "production's defaults were not read", which the same entry's new top text contradicts.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not P1 and not false: the clause is date-scoped to the 2026-09-16 baseline read, where production's defaults genuinely were not read, and the entry's new header states "Preflight on both: zero global pg_default_acl rows" (:2879). But the paragraph it closes is written in pre-apply imperative ("Before apply, ... must") and is labelled mandatory, so a later auditor of that paragraph alone can conclude the production preflight is still owed. The underlying fact is verified true three ways in this pass: neither committed pre-apply snapshot contains a single pg_default_acl row outside a named schema (all 300 rows are in auth/extensions/graphql/graphql_public/public/realtime/storage), the production-apply README records the PASS, and a live read-only query returned 0 rows with defaclnamespace = 0 on BOTH projects. Remedy is one clause: date-qualify or drop it. P2 because the worst action it can provoke is re-running a read-only query that returns 0.
